prize_parts.citation: For the development of palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling
For the development of base editing, programmable chemical conversion of single DNA bases without double-strand cleavage

statement.case_for: I have moved from nanopore sequencing (B039) to a two-part configuration of C-N cross-coupling (Buchwald and Hartwig) and base editing (Liu). Round 1 showed that B039 has no support beyond me and an unresolved three-name credit problem, and I should not hold a position only because it matches my own physical intuition. B023 offers what I look for in a physical sense: a clear mechanistic principle (ligand-controlled oxidative addition, amine binding and reductive elimination at palladium), quantitative understanding, a general capability that replaced harsh substrate-limited chemistry, and more than 25 years of independent confirmation, with a clean two-person credit. B060 is the achievement that members from several fields place on their ballots, with Liu named as the decisive originator in every statement that discusses it. It turns a defined deamination reaction into a programmable single-nucleotide chemical edit without double-strand cleavage, and it clearly opens unforeseen possibilities. The two parts are distinct achievements, one a classical molecule-making method and one a chemical-biology capability, and together use only three names.
statement.case_against: This is a pragmatic pairing rather than a thematically unified prize, and I will say so. B023 sits close to the 2010 cross-coupling prize, and Kosugi's 1983 tin-amide coupling is a real precursor that a two-name credit leaves out. B060 follows the 2020 CRISPR prize, its clinical record is short and long-term safety is unproven, and a single-name credit omits Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo and Nishida. If the committee decides that either part is a downstream extension of a recent prize, the configuration weakens. B039, which I previously preferred, is lost, and so is the enzyme-ratchet physics I find most convincing.

responses.point: B023 is a simple, general, mature method with a clean Buchwald and Hartwig credit that meets the test of a game-changer, and the 2010 overlap is the main objection.
responses.response: In round 1 I asked what principle was discovered beyond what C-C coupling already implied. Your account, and Somfai's, answers it well enough for me: the C-N step required its own ligand design (bulky alkylphosphines and biaryl phosphines) to make amine binding and C-N reductive elimination competitive with beta-hydride elimination, which C-C coupling did not predict. I treat the 2010 overlap as a mild concern rather than disqualifying, and on Kosugi I agree that the general catalytic method, not the stoichiometric-tin demonstration, is the decisive step. This moved me to support B023.

responses.point: B060 is a defined nucleic-acid deamination reaction made programmable and general, with Liu as the decisive originator, and it is better reproduced than most biology-facing candidates; you pair it with B041.
responses.response: I asked you in round 1 whether modified-base detection is a chemical advance, but my own concern now is yours: is B060 a separate discovery from the 2020 CRISPR prize? Your framing of it as a defined deamination reaction, now evolved to act on DNA, persuades me that it is chemistry distinct from Cas9 cleavage. I also accept your point that independent reproduction matters more than conceptual appeal. Where I differ is the partner. B041 still has an open scope question (PROTACs only or cereblon glues) and no approved degrader, which makes three names and a citation harder to defend than B023. I keep B041 as my first alternative.

responses.point: A prize of C-N coupling and base editing combines one traditional molecule-making achievement with one chemical-biology achievement, with only three names.
responses.response: I agree with the structure, and your own case against is accurate that it is a coalition rather than a unified theme. I would answer that the citation need not be unified, only that each part be defensible alone and explainable to a broad audience, which both are. On Kondo and Nishida, I accept that omitting them has a real cost, but their Target-AID work is a cytidine deaminase fusion that followed the deaminase-Cas concept, and the three-name limit makes Liu alone the better decision. I would like you to say whether you would accept adding Komor to B060 if a majority wanted it, at the cost of dropping nothing, since we would then be at four people.

responses.point: B030 is the one clean physical-mechanism case, but you concede that B023 is stronger and better supported and would not oppose it.
responses.response: I find the physical clarity of tunnelling in proteins attractive, as I said in round 1, and you have not yet named a dated key experiment to answer my question about when the decisive result occurred. Without that, I cannot weigh B030 against the clear priority of Buchwald and Hartwig. Since you say you would not oppose B023, I read your position as compatible with the B023 plus B060 configuration, which differs from yours only in replacing Gray and Winkler. I would ask you whether you can support that on its merits.

responses.point: B052 is a new organising principle grounded in physical chemistry, with Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen as founders.
responses.response: I still respect the concept, and your answer that the in vitro reconstitution and P-granule demonstrations stand independently of the in vivo dispute is the best form of the case. But the committee cannot cite the concept without addressing which cellular condensates are truly phase separated, and leaving out Pappu and Mittag is a visible cost under the three-person limit. I regard B052 as a candidate for later years rather than this one, and I would like to hear whether you would move to a second choice this year.

uncertainties: Whether B023 is judged distinct enough from the 2010 cross-coupling prize, and how much Kosugi's 1983 precedent should weigh.
Whether base editing is mature enough given its short clinical record, and whether Liu alone is the right credit or Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo or Nishida should be added within the three-person limit.
Whether a pairing of a classical method and a chemical-biology capability can be defended as a coherent public position.
Whether B041 (Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli) is a stronger second part than B060 for the members who place it first.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile. My research on molecular motors and Brownian ratchets is adjacent to the enzyme-ratchet step in B039, which I no longer include in my preferred configuration and now list only as an alternative; I have no connection to any name in B023 or B060. As chair, I have tried to base this move on the round-1 exchange and not to steer the committee.
